trap.segment: Specialty coffee enthusiasts (home baristas, specialty cafe regulars): 76% purchase intent but only 0.5 million adults, 1% of adults 18-64

items.quote: They are the largest group, with 11.4M adults (22% of adults 18-64) and 34% purchase intent.
Specialty coffee enthusiasts show 76% intent but number 0.5M, students show 41% at 2.6M, and office workers 27% at 8.9M.
The German chilled RTD coffee category was worth 610 million euros in 2024 and grew about 7% per year from 2021 to 2024; plant-based products hold 14% of it [1].
23% of adults bought chilled RTD coffee in the last 3 months [1].
By channel, supermarkets and discounters account for 54% of sales, petrol stations and convenience stores 24%, train-station and airport kiosks 13%, and online and other 9% [1].
The document calls Germany Europe's largest RTD coffee market and oat drinks its fastest-growing plant-based drink category [2].
The only German chilled RTD price point is Emmi Caffè Latte Macchiato at 2.99 euros per 230 ml cup [3].
One German retailer lists the Macchiato 230 ml at 2.99 euros (13.00 euros per litre), with multi-buy discounts down to 2.70 euros [3].
An Austrian retailer lists it at 1.99 euros [5], so prices vary a lot by retailer.
Starbucks Caffè Latte Eiskaffee 220 ml is listed in REWE's online shop; no price was visible [6].

One example is Aldi Nord's Moreno 'Typ Eiskaffee mit Milch', 275 g can, at 1.59 euros.

strategy_vs_analysis.reason: The plan chooses commuters (SEG2) on the basis of the segment table: 11.4M adults vs 0.5M enthusiasts, plus intent times size, and it ties the choice to the 3,500-point and 3% value share goals. Channels (petrol stations, convenience, kiosks, supermarkets) match the stated commuter purchase locations and the category channel split, and the pricing rationale explains the 2.49 euro hold against the only German price point.

campaign_vs_strategy.reason: Messages consistently speak to commuters with the positioning (no added sugar, vegan, organic, 18-hour cold brew) and use only the strategy's channels. Minor gap: the supermarket message ("Cold Brew aus Aarhus") is more about origin than the commuter pause, and the social channel's #MeinNordbrewMoment is a commute message but is generic about the target's on-the-go need.
